headline: Highest risk is medium: shared filesystem and permissive tool use create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways between Cline and Superset.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline can read/write workspace files, use MCP, and runs with no default isolation; Superset exposes an API surface and allowlisted egress. A shared filesystem or file handoff lets attacker-controlled content from one agent be parsed by the other as instructions. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default workspace setups, though not proven by docs.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace directory
IF one agent ingests file contents or MCP payloads as trusted instructions
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable MCP servers for untrusted content
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent files
Require manual review before one agent reads the other's outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline touches source code and browser screenshots and can write/read the filesystem; Superset has an API surface and allowlisted egress. If they share a workspace, sensitive code or screenshots can flow from Cline into Superset outputs or API calls. This is not critical because Superset's touched data classes are unspecified, but the shared-workspace leakage path is credible.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same files
IF Cline stores screenshots or code in shared paths
IF Superset exports or transmits those files through its API or egress
mitigations: Use separate OS users or containers
Keep screenshots and secrets out of shared folders
Restrict Superset API access to non-sensitive datasets
Turn off automatic file ingestion where possible

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline has unrestricted filesystem write and git-state modification, while Superset can call APIs and egress over allowlisted network paths. Overlapping writes to shared resources can race or overwrite each other, especially if both operate in the same workspace or repository. No locking mechanism is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents modify the same repository or directory
IF either agent writes configuration or generated artifacts without locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Pause one agent during the other's commit or export step
Review git diffs before merge

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate code, browser-derived facts, and file edits; Superset can consume APIs and produce analytics outputs. If Superset treats Cline's artifacts as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into dashboards, queries, or downstream actions. The interaction is plausible but not documented as fully automated, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Superset ingests files or API payloads produced by Cline
IF no validation step checks Cline's outputs before use
mitigations: Add a human verification gate
Require schema validation on imported artifacts
Mark Cline outputs as untrusted by default
Use read-only staging before production import

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not declare regulated data handling, residency, or retention constraints. Cline touches source code and screenshots, while Superset lists no data classes touched. With no stated compliance mismatch, only a low residual risk remains from undocumented deployment choices; the other agent is not cited because no specific compliance surface is declared for it.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into Cline's workspace
IF Superset is deployed under a stricter residency or retention policy than Cline
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools
Document retention settings
Review deployment region and logging defaults
Use separate environments for sensitive workloads
